dateline: New Delhi / Islamabad / Gilgit-Baltistan / Srinagar / United Nations — August 1947–Present
heroHeadline: Day 467: US Envoy Calls J&K 'Part of India' in Srinagar, Pakistan Summons Chargé d'Affaires; Delhi, Islamabad Trade Barricade Removals at Rival High Commissions
heroSubtitle: August 20, 2026: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor, on his first visit to J&K, told a joint briefing with CM Omar Abdullah in Srinagar (Aug 19) that Kashmir 'is an important part of India and an incredibly beautiful place,' drawing an immediate protest from Islamabad — Pakistan's Foreign Office summoned US Chargé d'Affaires Natalie Baker and lodged a 'strong demarche,' calling the remarks 'factually incorrect.' Separately, a tit-for-tat diplomatic exchange played out at the two countries' high commissions: Pakistan quietly removed parking poles and barricades outside the Indian High Commission in Islamabad around Aug 17, and India reciprocated on Aug 20 by demolishing unauthorised queue-management structures outside the Pakistan High Commission in Delhi. Pakistan also extended its airspace ban on Indian aircraft to Sept 24 (Aug 19) — the 16th consecutive NOTAM extension since April 2025. The ceasefire holds at Day 467 with no LOC violations since May 10, 2025. Bilateral freeze remains comprehensive: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT 'in abeyance.' This follows PM Sharif's Aug 14 warning that 'every single drop' of Pakistan's water is a red line, India's MEA rebuttal of 'no change' in its IWT stance, and the Aug 15 conclusion of Pakistan's drawn-out AJK Assembly election (PML-N 25 seats, PPP 12) after weeks of deadly JAAC reserved-seat protests.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
